regions.full_page: Feb. 8, 1914 Holy Trinity & St. Anthony's Septuagesima. And receiving it. They murmured against the householder (Luke VIII-5) Bel. Bro. One of the most immediate and necessary con- sequences of sin is discontentment. Therefore, it is that we are all more or less inclined to be discontented more or less inclined to complain because we are all more or less given to sin or inclined to sin. And the more we are inclined to sin, or the more we give way so it at least, the more do we become discontented and in- clined to murmur. History proves this from the time of Adam till the present day and will prove it till time and men are no more. Adam and Eve were contented and happy. They were at peace with themselves; at peace with all nature, at peace with the Creator, till they sinned. But, alas! they did not realize their privi- leges of innocence, their privilege of exemption from passion and death; their privilege of fidelity to Almighty God. They disobeyed Him. They sinned against Him. At once their peace was gone - peace of conscience peace of nature, peace with God. They were unhappy. They had ofended God. All nature feared them and was against them. They were discontented. They wandered away from the gardens and from the gates of Paradise. Their children inherited their sin and their posterity have followed them not only in sinning but also in the consequences thereof as well. They have been discon- tented, unhappy without peace or rest often murmuring in a sinful and blaspemous manner against the divine Householder - against God Himself. But this can be said not only of individuals, but of society in general of nations, of generaticos. Sin causes discontentment. Not only because society is made up of individuals and nations and generations in like manner but there are sins of society and national sins which bring their special curse to society or to the nation, e.g. cur own national s. education without religion - its fruit another national sin - divorce, the curse of the age! --
